title: Prayers on the Prophet ﷺ
hookLine: sending blessings on him, returned tenfold (Muslim)

lines: A SMALL SYMBOL AFTER HIS NAME.
cards: Every time the Prophet's name has appeared on your screen on this path, it's been followed by a small symbol, a knot of Arabic calligraphy. Maybe you wondered what it was. This week's words have mostly been for God.
Today's is still addressed to God, but it asks for someone else. Today: what that little symbol says.

teach.b: The symbol is short for sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam: may Allah send blessings on him and peace. Saying it, or any prayer like it, is called salawat, the plural of salah, the same word as prayer.
It's said when his name is spoken. Why?

teach.h: ALLAH AND HIS ANGELS SEND BLESSINGS.
teach.b: The Qur'an, in Surah al-Ahzab, says that Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet, and tells the believers: you, too, send blessings on him, and greet him with peace.
So a Muslim who says it is joining something already happening. The companions took this seriously enough to ask how.
A hadith in Bukhari says they came to him: we know how to greet you with peace, but how do we send blessings on you?
He taught them a prayer that begins: O Allah, send blessings on Muhammad and on the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings on Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim.
Many Muslims recite it in the last sitting of every prayer, just before the peace to both sides. Notice who's in it: Ibrahim, the friend of God, whose story you met in camp two. Then the promise.
In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet said: whoever sends one blessing on me, Allah sends ten blessings on them.

teach.h: ONE GOES OUT, TEN COME BACK.
teach.b: One goes out, ten come back. And a gentle rebuke.

teach.h: THE STINGY ONE HEARS AND IS SILENT.
teach.b: A hadith in Tirmidhi says the stingy one is the person who hears my name and doesn't send a blessing. Four words in Arabic, and holding them back earns that name.

how: Muslims say sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam whenever the Prophet is named, recite the prayer of blessings on Muhammad and Ibrahim in the last sitting of every prayer, and many increase their salawat on Fridays.

o: a prayer asking God to bless the Prophet
a thank-you said after finishing a meal
a prayer offered to the Prophet himself

games.q: what's inside the salawat — tap the pairs.
p: may Allah send blessings on him and peace
the prayer in the last sitting

s: the ﷺ symbol is just a decoration
it abbreviates sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam: may Allah send blessings on him and peace.
the Qur'an says Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet
Surah al-Ahzab, 33:56, and it asks the believers to do the same.
a hadith calls someone who hears his name and stays silent stingy

games.q: you're one of the companions. you know how to greet the Prophet ﷺ with peace, but not how to send blessings on him. what do you do?
o: ask him, and he teaches you a prayer
games.why: they asked, and he taught: O Allah, send blessings on Muhammad and his family, as You sent blessings on Ibrahim and his family (Bukhari).

practice: Rest your right hand, palm up, and count ten salawat, slowly: ten, not a hundred.

If you pray, say sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam on each count, or the longer prayer from the last sitting if you know it; if you don't, hold in mind the man the words are for, sent, Muslims say, as a mercy to the worlds, and count ten breaths.

wordCard.voice: Salawat. Blessings sent on the Prophet, the words behind the symbol; one sent, ten returned. Today's word, and a week of remembrance on your fingers.

orig.note: Arabic: may Allah send blessings on him and peace, written in short as ﷺ.

carryVoice: Your line: peace on him. Tomorrow, the path turns to a month: Ramadan, and the new moon. Day one hundred nineteen.
